questions.question: The tribal group called 'Santhals' rose in revolt in _______.
questions.solution:
The Santhal Rebellion (Santhal Hool) broke out in 1855 in the Rajmahal hills (present-day Jharkhand).
  • The movement was led by two brothers, Sidhu and Kanhu Murmu.
  • It was a revolt against the oppressive Zamindari system and British colonial exploitation.

questions.question: The Muttaraiyar held power in the Kaveri delta. They were subordinate to the Pallava kings of _______.
questions.solution:
The Muttaraiyar family held power in the Kaveri delta and served as subordinates to the Pallava kings of Kanchipuram.
  • Vijayalaya, from the Chola family, defeated the Muttaraiyar to establish the Chola Empire.
  • The Pallavas were famous for their rock-cut architecture, like the Shore Temple.

questions.question: ____________, who lived in the court of Kanishka, composed a biography of the Buddha, the Buddhacharita.
questions.solution:
Ashvaghosha composed the Buddhacharita, which is the biography of Buddha.
  • He lived in the court of Kanishka, the most famous Kushana ruler.
  • His work is considered a masterpiece of Sanskrit literature.

questions.question: Jallianwala Bagh massacre happened in 1919. Where is Jallianwala Bagh located?
questions.solution:
The Jallianwala Bagh massacre occurred on April 13, 1919, in Amritsar, Punjab.
  • Thousands had gathered to protest the Rowlatt Act and the arrest of leaders Saifuddin Kitchlew and Dr. Satyapal.
  • General Dyer ordered his troops to open fire on the unarmed crowd.

questions.question: Which organization was founded in 1867 in Bombay?
questions.solution:
The Prarthana Samaj was founded in 1867 in Bombay by Atmaram Pandurang.
  • It aimed at social and religious reforms like widow remarriage and women's education.
  • Prominent leaders like Mahadev Govind Ranade joined it later and expanded its influence.

questions.question: ______ was the capital of Magadha for several year before is was shifted to Pataliputra.
questions.solution:
Rajagriha (modern-day Rajgir in Bihar) was the first capital of Magadha.
  • It was naturally fortified by five hills.
  • The capital was later shifted to Pataliputra (Patna) by Udayin.

questions.question: Emperor Ashoka was the son of ________.
questions.solution:
Emperor Ashoka was the son of the second Mauryan emperor, Bindusara.
  • His mother's name was Subhadrangi.
  • Ashoka is remembered as one of the greatest rulers in Indian history for his propagation of 'Dhamma'.

questions.question: In ______, James Mill, a Scottish economist and political philosopher, published a massive three-volume work, A History of British India.
questions.solution:
In 1817, James Mill published 'A History of British India'.
  • He divided Indian history into three periods: Hindu, Muslim, and British.
  • He was a Scottish economist and political philosopher who never actually visited India.

questions.question: Sher Khan defeated Humayun at Chausa in ______.
questions.solution:
Sher Khan (Sher Shah Suri) defeated the Mughal Emperor Humayun in the Battle of Chausa in 1539.
  • Following this victory, Sher Khan assumed the title Sher Shah.
  • He later defeated Humayun again at the Battle of Kannauj (1540), forcing him into exile.

questions.question:
Which of the following was a provincial capital under the rule of Ashoka?
I. Taxila
II. Ujjain
questions.solution:
During the reign of Ashoka, both Taxila and Ujjain were important provincial capitals.
  • Taxila was a gateway to the northwest, while Ujjain lay on the route from north to south India.
  • Royal princes were often sent to these provinces as governors (Kumaras).

questions.question: Bahadur Shah Zafar and his sons were arrested by the British officials from __________ in Delhi.
questions.solution:
The last Mughal emperor, Bahadur Shah Zafar, and his sons were arrested from Humayun's Tomb in Delhi.
  • They were captured by Major William Hodson after the fall of Delhi in September 1857.
  • Bahadur Shah Zafar was later exiled to Rangoon, where he died in 1862.

questions.question: Which dynasty ruled over Delhi during 1290 to 1320?
questions.solution:
The Khalji Dynasty ruled the Delhi Sultanate from 1290 to 1320.
  • The dynasty was founded by Jalaluddin Khalji.
  • Its most powerful ruler was Alauddin Khalji, known for his market reforms and southern conquests.

questions.question: Who introduced the concept of poverty line in pre-independent India?
questions.solution:
Dadabhai Naoroji, known as the 'Grand Old Man of India', was the first to discuss the concept of the poverty line in India.
  • He used the 'jail cost of living' as a basis for his calculations.
  • He authored the book 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India', detailing the 'Drain of Wealth' theory.

questions.question: The Shunga dynasty was established by whom among the following rulers?
questions.solution:
The Shunga dynasty was established by Pushyamitra.
  • He was a military general who usurped the throne from the Mauryas.
  • He is often credited with the revival of Vedic traditions in India.

questions.question: In February _____, Mahatma Gandhi decided to withdraw the Non-Cooperation Movement.
questions.solution:
Mahatma Gandhi withdrew the Non-Cooperation Movement in February 1922.
  • The withdrawal was prompted by the Chauri Chaura incident, where a mob set fire to a police station.
  • Gandhi believed the movement was turning violent and the people were not yet ready for a non-violent struggle.

questions.question: General Dyer took command during the martial law in which year?
questions.solution:
General Dyer assumed command in Amritsar and imposed martial law in April 1919.
  • Under martial law, public gatherings were banned, leading to the tragic Jallianwala Bagh massacre.
  • This event was a turning point in India's struggle for independence.

questions.question: Which of the following archaeological sites is NOT located in present day India?
questions.solution:
Mehrgarh is an important Neolithic site located in the Kachi Plain of Balochistan, Pakistan, not in present-day India.
  • It is considered one of the earliest sites with evidence of farming and herding in South Asia.
  • Sites like Chirand (Bihar) and Hallur (Karnataka) are located in modern India.

questions.question: Which among the following is the oldest vedas?
questions.solution:
The Rigveda is the oldest of the four Vedas, dating back to approximately 1500–1000 BCE.
  • The other three are the Samaveda, Yajurveda, and Atharvaveda.
  • It primarily consists of prayers offered to deities like Agni, Indra, and Soma.

questions.question: There were men and women such as the__________, who did not own land in post Mauryan Period.
questions.solution:
In the post-Mauryan period, Dasa Karmakara referred to landless laborers who worked on the fields of others.
  • Grihapatis were small, independent landowners.
  • In South India, large landowners were known as Vellalar.

questions.question: Torgya, a ________ -day monastery festival, is observed by the Monpa tribe of Arunachal Pradesh.
questions.solution:
Torgya is a three-day religious festival celebrated by the Monpa tribe at the Tawang Monastery in Arunachal Pradesh.
  • It is held to chase away evil spirits and pray for prosperity.
  • The festival features the famous 'Chham' (masked dance) performed by monks.

questions.question: Name the Bengali reformer and book writer who supported widow remarriage.
questions.solution:
Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar was a great reformer who tirelessly advocated for widow remarriage.
  • His efforts led to the passing of the Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act, 1856.
  • He was also a key figure in modernizing Bengali prose.

questions.question: Charaka is known as the father of __________.
questions.solution:
Charaka is hailed as the 'Father of Ayurveda'.
  • He was the court physician of King Kanishka.
  • He wrote the Charaka Samhita, a fundamental text on ancient Indian medicine.

questions.question: Veer Lakhan Nayak, a legendary tribal leader from __________ participated in Quit India Movement and was hanged by the Britishers in 1943.
questions.solution:
Veer Lakhan Nayak was a tribal leader from Orissa who played a significant role in the Quit India Movement.
  • He was a member of the Bhuyan tribe.
  • He was executed by the British at the Berhampur Jail in 1943.

questions.question: The Indian National Congress was founded in:
questions.solution:
The Indian National Congress (INC) was founded in 1885.
  • The first session was held in Bombay and was attended by 72 delegates.
  • Retired British official A.O. Hume played a major role in its formation.

questions.question: At the age of__________, Mahavira left home and went to live in a forest in search of enlightenment.
questions.solution:
At the age of thirty, Mahavira (Vardhamana) left his home and royal life in search of spiritual truth.
  • He attained enlightenment (Kevala Jnana) after 12 years of intense penance.
  • He was the 24th Tirthankara of Jainism.
